prompt.context: The year is 1990 and your client is the CEO of Rolls Royce ('RR'). He is worried about his business, as he has seen a sharp decline in the demand for luxury cars (there was a global slowdown/recession in the early 1990s). RR was selling 3500 cars per year and is now selling at a run rate of 1100 cars per year. As you can imagine, RR faces high fixed costs as it attempts to keep plants running (due to the expense involved with shutting down plants and laying off unionized workers). This has resulted in an increase in inventory — now 1000 cars are in finished goods. RR is running at an operating loss of about $1M per week and is cash flow negative. They are owned by a small conglomerate of unrelated businesses. Keep in mind that (1) the economy is deteriorating, (2) we don't have the time or money to fully develop new products, and (3) Mercedes and BMW are spending more money than we are on R&D and sales and marketing.
prompt.question: We were asked to develop a turnaround strategy for Rolls Royce. How would you go about thinking about this?

clarifying_info.q: What is the ownership structure of Rolls Royce?
clarifying_info.a: RR is owned by a small conglomerate of unrelated businesses.

clarifying_info.q: Is developing new products an option?
clarifying_info.a: No — we don't have the time or money to fully develop new products.

clarifying_info.q: What is the current financial situation?
clarifying_info.a: RR is running at an operating loss of about $1M per week and is cash flow negative. Finished goods inventory has built up to 1000 cars.

framework: Revenue: Optimize the core business (pricing, volume/bundling, product mix) and expand the business (new customer segments, new geographies, new distribution channels)
Costs: Map the value chain — commodity inputs/parts, PP&E, labor, sales & marketing, overhead, distribution — and identify where to cut
Inventory: Determine optimal finished-goods inventory level given current demand, demand variability, model/customization complexity, and production lead times
Recommendation: Prioritize the highest-impact levers given constraints (no new products, deteriorating economy, limited R&D budget) and provide a clear action plan

questions.prompt: Phase 1 — Revenue: How would you think about increasing revenues for Rolls Royce under these constraints?
questions.guidance: Candidate should structure revenue into two buckets: (1) Optimizing the core business and (2) Expanding the business. For the core: price (RR customers are relatively price-insensitive, so there is a case for raising prices; alternatively, lower prices to compete), volume/bundling (increase marketing/promotion spend, bundle extended warranties and/or repairs with cars), product mix (push the most profitable models). For expansion: new products are off the table, so focus on new markets — new customer segments, new geographies, or new distribution channels. The candidate should demonstrate structured thinking and good prioritization given the constraints.

questions.prompt: Phase 2 — Cost Cutting: What are the major cost components of this business and how could we find ways to make cuts?
questions.guidance: Candidate should use the value chain as a structure: commodity inputs (parts), PP&E expense, labor (especially union-related costs), sales and marketing, overhead, and distribution. Top priorities to cut are labor and distribution costs, followed by sales and marketing. Marketing could be focused on just the wealthiest customers during the downturn. For labor, the candidate should suggest: reducing the number of cars produced and cutting line staff, reducing support/overhead staff, and cutting sales reps — without eliminating capabilities needed for recovery.

questions.prompt: Phase 3 — Inventory: If we cut car production, what factors would affect the optimal level of finished goods inventory?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify: (1) the overall level of demand, (2) the variability of demand, (3) the number of car models and degree of customization (higher customization = lower ability to hold generic inventory), and (4) the lead time necessary to produce another batch of vehicles (longer lead time = higher safety stock needed). Additional factors such as carrying costs, storage costs, and working capital constraints are also valid.

brainstorming.prompt: How could Rolls Royce explore new markets to expand revenues, given they cannot develop new products?

categories.name: New Customer Segments
ideas: Target newly wealthy entrepreneurs or emerging high-net-worth individuals

categories.name: New Geographies
ideas: Enter emerging luxury markets in Asia or the Middle East
Target markets where luxury car penetration is still low
Partner with local distributors in underpenetrated regions

categories.name: New Distribution Channels
ideas: Partnerships with luxury hotels or chauffeur services
Enhanced dealer network in high-wealth zip codes

recommendation: Implement an immediate cost-reduction program focused on labor (reduce production volume to match ~1100 cars/year run rate) and distribution, while protecting core brand capabilities
On the revenue side, consider modest price increases (leveraging brand inelasticity) and bundle value-added services (warranties, repairs) to maintain revenue per unit
Explore new geographic markets and customer segments to broaden demand without requiring new product development
Manage down the 1000-car finished goods inventory through targeted promotions or fleet/corporate sales
risks: Cutting too deeply into labor could impair quality and damage the Rolls Royce brand
Macroeconomic deterioration may worsen faster than cost cuts can offset
Competitors (Mercedes, BMW) with higher R&D and marketing budgets may gain further share during the downturn
next_steps: Quantify the cost savings from reducing production to 1100 units/year and identify which plants/lines to consolidate
Model the break-even volume at the restructured cost base
Assess specific geographic markets for near-term entry with minimal investment
Develop a plan to sell down finished-goods inventory of 1000 cars
